==Broken quote template==
The simplest syntax for using [[Template:Quote]] is <nowiki>{{quote|text of quote|citation}}</nowiki>. This may NOT be altered to <nowiki>{{quote|'''color'''|text of quote|citation}}</nowiki>, or it will break tons of pages, [http://wot.wikia.com/index.php?title=Lan_Mandragoran&action=purge like this one].

By the way, I've grown increasingly dissatisfied with the complexity of Template:Quote. First someone added borders, now you're adding colors? It's purpose is to serve up simple, straightforward, legible quotations--not serve as a page decorator. I liked how it was [http://wot.wikia.com/index.php?title=Template:Quote&oldid=12992 as of May 2007], before Moridin changed it last February. --[[User:Gherald|Gherald]] 19:28, 5 August 2009 (UTC)

: Alright I will change it back. I was trying to see if it would work. It doesn't really.. my bad.--[[User:Optimous|Optimous]] 19:30, 5 August 2009 (UTC)

:: If you really want to add colors, parameters 1-3 are taken, you'd have to start with parameter 4, or, preferably, used a new named parameter such as color=.
:: You can add that if you want, but I don't get the point of having all this complex formatting (borders, color, and centering at top of page instead of left-adjusted like it used to be) --[[User:Gherald|Gherald]] 19:34, 5 August 2009 (UTC)
::: It doesn't work because of the link color. Also it I realize it looks WAY to flashy. Classic is better :)--[[User:Optimous|Optimous]] 19:36, 5 August 2009 (UTC)

== Random numbers ==

I created [[Template:Random]], which you can subst anywhere you want a random number. I'm thinking this would be useful fo displaying random quotes on the main page, instead of having to choose a particularone for every day.

Suppose we've gathered 30 quotes. We can put them all in one page template page with a switch statement that picks one to display, or, if you prefer, have a Q# page for each one like the FAs. Then you can use <nowiki>{{subst:random|30}}</nowiki> to either choose something from the switch template or transclude the corresponding Q# page.

We could even display a random FA, instead of being limited to 1 per month day. --[[User:Gherald|Gherald]] 22:59, 6 August 2009 (UTC)
:Oh, one problem with the approach...the random number won't change until the page is edited/purged. Rats. I suppose I could write a clientform script that logs me in and requests a purge at least once/day...gotta think about this. --[[User:Gherald|Gherald]] 23:01, 6 August 2009 (UTC)
::Ah also would this be different for everyone is in a different random number for each person viewing the page or would it be a global thing that everyone would see the same quote and FA? Another thing wouldn't this mean that the same FA or quote could be chosen twice in a row?
::: It's the same for all until page is edited/purged. And yes, the same random number could be chosen in more than one consecutive edit/purge, but that's not an issue.

And lastly Opti and optical do start the same but don't sound the same. Same goes with mous and moose. The name was split there only because it is half of the word on each side.--[[User:Optimous|<span style="color:blue;">OPTI</span>]][[User_talk:Optimous|<span style="color:red;">MOUS</span>]] 09:57, January 22, 2010 (UTC)

== Request for adminship ==

To start, I am extremely hesitant to post this at all. For me, personally, I have never liked self-nominations. I have always thought that they were too self-promoting. However, I am also of the opinion that a wiki cannot have too many admins. 

As the most active admin on the site, I decided to come to you first. I have had more interaction with you than the other admins and feel more comfortable coming to you. I mean no disrespect to either [[User:Gherald|Gherald]] nor [[User:Nae'blis|Nae'blis]] as bureaucrats of this wiki, nor to the other admins, [[User:Moridin 2000|Moridin]] and [[User:TheParanoidOne|TheParanoidOne]]. I have a great respect for you all.

Some wiki's do not allow self-nominations and some do. This wiki does not have a formal admin nomination forum. As such, I would like ask that the current admins review my edits and consider me as an admin for this wiki. 

I would also like to ask that any editor of this wiki, whether the newest-registered or long-time contributor, add his or her opinion here to whether they believe I would be a good administrator.

As for why, I can only submit the following: 
*I belive that I can fulfill the role of an admin on this wiki. 
*I have made several significant contributions to this wiki and I will continue to make similar contributions in the future. 
*There have been several pages and templates that I have either created or updated that have had significant impact across the wiki.

Any criticism of my edits is welcome and appriciated. Any opposition to my nomination is also welcome.

Optimous, I would like to thank you for the "hosting" of these proceedings. If you believe that this could be better covered or more appropriate at another page, by all means, move this post there.

As always, honor to serve. ----[[User:Mainphramephreak|<span style="color:#000099;"> '''Willie'''</span>]] - [[User Talk:Mainphramephreak|<span style="color:#990099;">'''''HtS'''''</span>]] 07:45, February 20, 2010 (UTC)

The only thing is I can't promote you. Only Nae'blis or Gherald can promote. And since they haven't been active for a while it could be a little while before you can be promoted. I don't have their emails so I can't send them a request.  But you have definitely put the effort to be an admin.  Keep up the good work.--[[User:Optimous|<span style="color:blue;">OPTI</span>]][[User_talk:Optimous|<span style="color:red;">MOUS</span>]] 12:27, February 20, 2010 (UTC)

== Expansion of the Character template ==

So, in creating and editing a few characters from {{ns}}, something occurred to me. A lot of the characters from that book and the first few are kind of one-time characters. I think that the status of "Alive" could be kind of misleading/confusing. 

What do you think of adding "Last mentioned" and "Last appeared" fields to the character template? Same kind of rules from the first mentions/appeared would apply. "Last appeared" if that is the last time we've seen them, and adding "Last mentioned" if they were subsequently mentioned by another character, so that the "flow" would be first mentioned, first appeared, last appeared, last mentioned.

Do you think that it might also be feasable to categorize them? As in "Alive as of TGS" or "Alive (as of TGS)" or some such. 

I think that this should be hashed out/discussed before implementing it. Thoughts and ideas? ----[[User:Mainphramephreak|<span style="color:#000099;"> '''Willie'''</span>]] - [[User Talk:Mainphramephreak|<span style="color:#990099;">'''''HtS'''''</span>]] 19:03, July 16, 2010 (UTC)
:Hmm. Yeah I think that would be a good idea since I have myself saw characters that said alive when they were mentioned in NS and we have never heard of them again. The last appeared would have like the others right? Like {{TGS|30}} kinda thing right? So how would we categorize it?--[[User:Optimous|<span style="color:blue;">OPTI</span>]][[User_talk:Optimous|<span style="color:red;">MOUS</span>]] 19:12, July 16, 2010 (UTC)

I a perfect world (''where I could tell my computer to do exactly what I want it to do in plain English and have it understand me'') I would say that characters with one of the fields filled in would be included in the category "Alive (as of TGS)". So, last appeared in {{TGS|30}} would be in the same category as last appeared in {{TGS|1}} and so on. Can this be easily integrated in the character template, I'm not sure. I think it will be the chapter identifier in the <nowiki>{{book|chapter}}</nowiki> template that might give us problems. If it doesn't give us problems, then it should be a simple addition to the character template (and subsequent addition of those fields on the thousand or so character pages) and we'd be in business. If it does give us problems, a second template could be created using coding that switches {{TGS|1}}, {{TGS|2}}, ''ad nauseam'' with whatever the character template needs to properly categorize it. Trying to do all of the switches for 500+ chapters in the character template would add even more clutter than is already there. Does that make sense or do I need to get another cup of coffee? :):) 

Something else that just occured to me as well. Can we have these two new fields read the "status" field to determine whether the person is alive or dead? Since the two new fields would conceivably be used on characters that are dead, it would be kind of counterproductive to have the person in the "Dead" category as well as "Alive (as of TGS)". Case in point: Asmodean. Dead as of TFoH, but mentioned after that. Gotta love complications. :)----[[User:Mainphramephreak|<span style="color:#000099;"> '''Willie'''</span>]] - [[User Talk:Mainphramephreak|<span style="color:#990099;">'''''HtS'''''</span>]] 19:31, July 16, 2010 (UTC)

Conducted a few tests. It looks like we will have to have another template do the switching. I've written one, but I won't upload it until I can figure out how to integrate it into the character template. More to come. :) ----[[User:Mainphramephreak|<span style="color:#000099;"> '''Willie'''</span>]] - [[User Talk:Mainphramephreak|<span style="color:#990099;">'''''HtS'''''</span>]] 20:34, July 16, 2010 (UTC)

Another thing that occured to me. The "Last Mentioned" needs to take precedence over "Last Appeared" where the last mention of a character is in a later book than their last appearence. Case in point: Morgase. Last appeared in {{Kod|30}}, but mentioned in {{Tgs|47}}. She should only be categorized in "Alive (as of TGS)". Do you know of a way to supress the categorization of one of the fields based on the inclusion of another? If we can figure out how to have the status field supress the inclusion of "Alive (as of XXX)", then we can also use that same coding for this one. I've included the fields in the character template, but not the categorization yet. :) ----[[User:Mainphramephreak|<span style="color:#000099;"> '''Willie'''</span>]] - [[User Talk:Mainphramephreak|<span style="color:#990099;">'''''HtS'''''</span>]] 14:23, July 19, 2010 (UTC)

:Wait she should only be in the category TGS alive and not KOD or only KOD because she should be mentioned about being dead? Also would last mentioned always appear after last appeared? Because what if the character is around then leaves for a book or 2 but isn't mentioned? So would the mentioned and last appeared be the same? We can have like if {last mentioned} is not equal to {last appeared} put in category Alive (as of {last mentioned})--[[User:Optimous|<span style="color:blue;">OPTI</span>]][[User_talk:Optimous|<span style="color:red;">MOUS</span>]] 17:36, July 19, 2010 (UTC)

Morgase should be categorized as "Alive as of TGS" because that was the last time she was mentioned. The thing is, the coding would be present in both the "Last mentioned" and "Last appeared" fields and we would have to find someway of suppressing the "Last appeared" if a "Last mentioned" is present.

Yes, last mentioned would appear after last appeared. The flow would be: First mentioned => First appeared => Last appeared => Last mentioned.

The same rule we use for the firsts would be used for the lasts. For example, if the last time we see a character is also the last time they are mentioned in the books, only the "Last appeared" field would be used. To use Egwene as an example, the last time she is mentioned in the series is also the last time she appeares, so she would only get the "Last appeared" field. 

Basically, we need the two new fields to "read" the "status" field to detirmine if the character is alive. So:

*If status=Dead, then "L.A." and "L.M." do not categorize
*If status=Unknown/Debateable, then (I'm not sure, thoughts?)
*If status=Alive, then
**If "L.A." is used an not "L.M.", then categorize per "L.A." field
**If "L.A." and/or "L.M." is used, then categorize per "L.M." field
